roads.name: Chemin du Cap-Bon-Ami
words: Sweeping and steady: 10 curves in 2.3 miles.
From 13 to 370 ft, with 463 ft of up and down along the way.
roads.ratingNote: A full bar is top marks for that part; the percentages are each part's share of the rating. Curves, length and up and down are ranked against every road in the library. The rest are scored on the road itself: how few side roads join it, whether the curves or the limit set the pace, and how little is built up along it. At the 30 km/h limit its curves ask for about 0.13 g.

roads.name: Route des Failles
words: Properly twisty: 20 curves in 3.0 miles, about 7 a mile.
Plenty of tight curves among them.
From 151 to 898 ft, with 1,408 ft of up and down along the way.
roads.ratingNote: A full bar is top marks for that part; the percentages are each part's share of the rating. Curves, length and up and down are ranked against every sweeper in the library. The rest are scored on the road itself: how few side roads join it, whether the curves or the limit set the pace, and how little is built up along it. At the 90 km/h limit its corners still ask for about 1.31 g, so the curves, not the limit, set the pace. Most of it has no posted limit on the map, so this takes Quebec's 90 km/h.

roads.name: Route 132 Est
words: Sweeping and steady: 20 curves in 4.9 miles.
From 23 to 475 ft, with 1,625 ft of up and down along the way.
11 parks, trailheads and other stops along it, so it's likely busier than most, especially on weekends.
